case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: American Civil Liberties Union of Arizona v. Arizona Department of Child Safety
key_cases.holding: The court of appeals held that the electronic records and data DCS maintains in its CHILDS case-management system are public records subject to Arizona's public records law, affirming in part, reversing in part, and remanding.
key_cases.relevance: Makes the agency's own case-management data reachable by outside oversight and audit requests.
key_cases.quote: Under any of the formulations of a public record discussed above, and based on its content, CHILDS is a public record.

key_cases.holding: The Arizona Supreme Court held that purely personal documents of a public officer are not public records but that the custodian's assertion is not conclusive, reversed the superior court, vacated the court of appeals' opinion, and remanded for in camera inspection.
key_cases.relevance: Supplies the presumption of disclosure that oversight bodies and the public rely on to obtain agency records.
key_cases.quote: Arizona law defines "public records" broadly and creates a presumption requiring the disclosure of public documents

key_cases.case_name: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community v. Rogers
key_cases.holding: The Arizona Supreme Court vacated the superior court's disclosure order, holding that a document is not a public record merely because a public officer possesses it and that it must bear some relation to the officer's official duties, and ordering the tribal check distribution list returned.
key_cases.relevance: The foundational Arizona Supreme Court definition of what counts as a public record, which fixes the outer boundary of an oversight body's or requester's reach into agency files.
key_cases.quote: a public record must also have some relation to the official duties of the public officer that holds the record

key_cases.holding: The Arizona Supreme Court approved the court of appeals' decision and held that records a public officer is required to keep are presumed open to inspection, subject to the custodian's discretion to deny access where confidentiality, privacy, or the best interest of the state outweighs disclosure, with any such refusal subject to judicial scrutiny.
key_cases.relevance: The source of the presumption of openness that lets oversight bodies and the public demand agency records without first proving entitlement.
key_cases.quote: all records required to be kept under A.R.S. § 39-121.01(B), are presumed open to the public for inspection as public records

key_cases.case_name: Silverman v. Arizona Department of Economic Security
key_cases.holding: The Arizona Supreme Court held that investigative journalists can qualify as persons conducting 'bona fide research' under the confidentiality statute's exception, vacated the court of appeals' opinion, and remanded for the agency to exercise its release discretion under the definition the Court supplied.
key_cases.relevance: Shows how outside researchers and journalists can lawfully obtain protective-services records that seed oversight inquiries.
key_cases.quote: The primary issue before us is whether investigative journalists can engage in "bona fide research." We conclude they can.

mandatory_reporters: Physicians, physician assistants, optometrists, dentists, osteopathic physicians, chiropractors, podiatrists, behavioral health professionals, nurses, psychologists, counselors and social workers who form the belief while treating a patient — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(1)
Peace officers, child welfare investigators, child safety workers, members of the clergy, priests and Christian Science practitioners — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(2)
The parent, stepparent or guardian of the minor — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(3)
School personnel, including substitute teachers, and domestic violence or sexual assault victim advocates who form the belief in the course of their employment — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(4)
Any other person who has responsibility for the care or treatment of the minor — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(5)
Immediate or next-higher-level supervisors and administrators of a person listed in (A)(1), (2), (4) or (5) — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(6)
Members of a school district governing board or charter school governing body — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(7)
reporting_details: In Arizona a person listed in A.R.S. § 13-3620(A) must report immediately, electronically or by telephone, to a peace officer, to the Department of Child Safety, or — for an Indian minor who resides on an Indian reservation — to a tribal law enforcement or social services agency (A.R.S. § 13-3620(A), (D)).

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: A.R.S. § 8-456 states no penalty; the report must still reach the court 48 hours before a dependency hearing or within 21 days after a dependency petition is filed (A.R.S. § 8-456(F)(3)(b)).
